questions.question: What should you do at an intersection with a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Wait for the green light before going.
Slow down and cross carefully.
Stop before crossing.

questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and be careful. Watch for other traffic and pedestrians.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, you should:

options.text: Be ready for a person or vehicle to suddenly move into your lane.
Assume other drivers and pedestrians will see you.
Drive close to the parked cars to leave room for moving traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for a person or vehicle to suddenly move into your lane.
questions.explanation: Keep distance between your car and parked cars. A person may step out without looking. A driver may start moving without seeing you.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No U-turn.
No turning.
No left turn.

questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot make a U-turn. You cannot turn around to go the opposite direction.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Do not enter.
No parking.
No U-turn.

questions.explanation: This sign means no U-turn allowed. You cannot turn around to go the opposite direction.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Watch for people crossing.
No passing zone.
Work zone ahead.

questions.explanation: This orange warning sign tells you roadwork is coming. Stay alert for temporary traffic signs in work zones.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Do not enter.
Stop ahead.
Roadwork or maintenance ahead.

questions.explanation: Orange diamond signs mark construction and maintenance areas. They help you drive safely through these zones. Traffic fines may be higher in these areas.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn.
You must turn right.
Watch for traffic on your right.

questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right at this location.

questions.question: Traffic is merging into your lane on the freeway. You should:

options.text: Make room for them if you can.
Speed up to keep your position.
Always stay in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make room for them if you can.
questions.explanation: When possible, make room for merging vehicles.

questions.question: If you park your vehicle in an unusual spot, you should:

options.text: Turn on your reverse lights.
Make sure drivers can see your car from all directions.
Park five feet from the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure drivers can see your car from all directions.
questions.explanation: Your parked car should be visible to drivers coming from any direction so it does not become a hazard.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: One lane ahead.
Merging traffic ahead.
Lane ends ahead.

questions.explanation: This sign warns that traffic may merge into your lane ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Look only in the direction you are going, then go.
Let all vehicles go first, no matter when they arrive.
Look in all directions before going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look in all directions before going.
questions.explanation: At a stop sign, you must come to a full stop. Look all around for traffic before you go.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Do not drink and drive.
Road is slippery when wet.
Road curves ahead.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They tell you about conditions right ahead. This sign warns that the road becomes slippery when it is wet.

questions.question: What is the right way to enter an expressway from the entrance ramp?

options.text: Go down the ramp and move to your lane as quickly as possible.
Use the acceleration lane to match traffic speed and merge safely.
Go to the bottom of the ramp and stop completely before entering.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the acceleration lane to match traffic speed and merge safely.
questions.explanation: Use the acceleration lane next to the main road. Speed up in this lane until you are going the same speed as the expressway traffic. Then it is safe to merge into traffic.

questions.question: Do not start across an intersection if the light will turn red before you finish crossing:

options.text: Never do this.
It is okay if you entered on a yellow light.
It is okay if you entered on a green light.

questions.explanation: Never enter an intersection unless you can cross it completely before the light turns red. Blocking the intersection can result in a ticket.

questions.question: When weather or light is bad and you need your lights on while driving:

options.text: Use parking lights.
Use high beams.
Use low beams.

questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, snow, or rain. High beam lights bounce back and create glare, making it harder to see.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing, you must:

options.text: Watch for vehicles that must stop at railroad crossings, like school buses and hazmat trucks.
Watch for trains coming from both directions.
Both A and B.

questions.explanation: Approach all railroad crossings carefully. Cross only when no train is coming from either direction. Also watch for vehicles like school buses and hazmat trucks that must stop at crossings.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Cars in the right lane must slow down.
No left turn.
Traffic is merging.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign tells you that traffic from the right may merge into your lane. Be ready to let them in safely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow down and be ready to stop if cars are coming.
Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
Go carefully through the intersection without always stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: An octagon sign always means stop. Come to a complete stop at the stop line. If there is no stop line, stop before the crosswalk. Then go only when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Do not enter.
Give up the right-of-way.
Parking for people with disabilities.

questions.explanation: This sign is placed on one-way streets and roads where you cannot enter. You may see it if you try to go the wrong way on an expressway ramp.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Intersection ahead.
Merging traffic.
Steep hill ahead.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to conditions you may not see right away. This sign warns of a steep hill ahead. Slow down to avoid crashes and brake damage.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Steep grade ahead.
The road ahead has curves and turns.
Slippery when wet.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to possible dangers. This sign warns you that the road becomes slippery when wet. Drive carefully in rainy conditions.

questions.question: A police officer directs you to go through a red traffic light. What should you do?

options.text: Stop until the light turns green.
Go through the intersection without stopping.
Come to a complete stop before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go through the intersection without stopping.
questions.explanation: Always follow a police officer's directions. Their instructions override traffic signals and signs.

questions.question: When should you be most careful when turning or stopping in rainy weather?

options.text: After it has been raining all day.
One half hour after the rain stops.
During the first half hour of rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: During the first half hour of rain.
questions.explanation: Be extra careful during the first half hour of rain. Oil from cars mixes with the rain and makes the road very slippery.

questions.question: You see a deep puddle on the road ahead. What should you do?

options.text: Keep your speed to drive through the water quickly.
Avoid the puddle if possible.
Put the car in neutral while driving through the water.

questions.explanation: Avoid slippery areas like puddles, ice, wet leaves, and oil. The safest surface for driving is dry and solid.

questions.question: Which statement is correct?

options.text: Use your left foot to brake.
Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating.
Always brake hard to ensure you stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating.
questions.explanation: Use your right foot for both the brake and gas pedal. Brake gently with steady pressure so your car stops smoothly.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Be ready for traffic to merge into your lane.
Always stop.
Divided highway ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for traffic to merge into your lane.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns that traffic will merge from the right. Be ready to let them in safely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The height from the road to a bridge or overpass.
The maximum height a vehicle can be in this state.
The maximum width of a vehicle allowed on the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: The height from the road to a bridge or overpass.
questions.explanation: This sign warns of low clearance. It shows the distance from the road surface to the bottom of a bridge or overpass.

questions.question: You are merging onto an interstate highway. What should you do?

options.text: Find a safe gap and merge into traffic.
Cross two lanes at once.
Always stop before entering the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Find a safe gap and merge into traffic.
questions.explanation: Find a gap in traffic that is large enough for you to merge safely. Do not stop on the entrance ramp unless there is no safe gap to enter.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Come to a complete stop.
Keep going while looking and listening for trains.
Slow down, look both ways, listen for trains, and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, look both ways, listen for trains, and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing, slow down and look both ways. Listen for any trains and be prepared to stop if you see or hear one. Never try to outrun a train.

questions.question: A large truck ahead is turning right onto a street with two lanes in each direction. What might the truck do?

options.text: Turn into either of the two lanes.
Swing wide to complete the right turn.
Stay only in the right lane while turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Swing wide to complete the right turn.
questions.explanation: The rear wheels of a truck follow a shorter path than the front wheels. Long trucks need extra space to turn right. They often swing wide to complete the turn safely.
